title_tag: Long-Term Water Storage: What CDC Guidance Says | Final Vestige
meta_description: How long can stored water last? Official guidance: replace water you fill yourself every six months. Containers, cleaning, labels and storage, from the CDC and Ready.gov.
h1_option: Long-term water storage: containers, cleaning and the six-month rule
dek_option: Official guidance gives a rotation cycle, not a shelf life. Which containers are safe, how to sanitize them, where to keep them and when to replace the water, from the CDC and FEMA, with our reasoning kept separate.

faq.q: How much water should I store?
faq.a: The CDC says to store at least 1 gallon of water per person per day for 3 days, and to try for a 2-week supply if possible. Ready.gov says at least one gallon per person per day for several days, for drinking and sanitation.

faq.q: How long can stored water last?
faq.a: The official guidance gives a rotation cycle, not a shelf life. The CDC says to replace water in containers you filled yourself every six months and to observe the expiration date on store-bought water. Ready.gov says water that has not been commercially bottled should be replaced every six months. Neither page gives a longer period.

faq.q: What is the safest water to store?
faq.a: The CDC calls unopened, commercially bottled water the safest and most reliable source of water in an emergency. Ready.gov says to keep it in the sealed original container in a cool, dark place.

faq.q: What containers can I use to store water?
faq.a: The CDC says it is best to use FDA-approved food-grade water storage containers. If you cannot, choose a container with a tightly closing top, made of durable, unbreakable material (not glass), with a narrow neck or opening if possible. Do not use containers that previously held toxic chemicals such as bleach or pesticides.

faq.q: How do I clean a container before storing water?
faq.a: The CDC says to wash it with soap and rinse completely, sanitize it with 1 teaspoon of unscented liquid household chlorine bleach (5% to 9% sodium hypochlorite) in 1 quart (4 cups) of water, cover and shake, wait at least 30 seconds, pour the solution out and let the container dry before filling.

faq.q: Where should I keep stored water?
faq.a: The CDC says to keep containers in a cool place, 50°F to 70°F, away from direct sunlight and away from toxic substances such as gasoline or pesticides. Label each container "drinking water" with the storage date.
